subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When blood glucose falls too low, the pancreas releases glucagon, which causes the liver to:
questions.explain: Glucagon makes the liver convert stored glycogen back into glucose, raising blood glucose levels.

questions.q: Compared with a conscious response, a spinal reflex is:
options: Faster because it bypasses conscious brain processing
The same speed but uses more neurones
Slower and decided by the brain
questions.explain: Reflexes are faster than conscious responses because they do not pass through the conscious brain.

questions.q: In the menstrual cycle, a surge of which hormone triggers ovulation?
questions.explain: A surge in LH at around day 14 stimulates the release of an egg (ovulation).

questions.q: The relay neurone is found mainly in the:
questions.explain: Relay neurones are located in the CNS and connect sensory neurones to motor neurones.

questions.q: In the reflex arc, what is the 'effector'?
options: The receptor that detects the stimulus
A muscle or gland that produces the response
The relay neurone in the spinal cord
questions.explain: An effector is a muscle or gland that carries out the response, such as a muscle contracting.

questions.q: Which hormone lowers blood glucose concentration when it rises too high?
questions.explain: Insulin, released by the pancreas, causes cells to take up glucose and the liver to store it as glycogen, lowering blood glucose.

options: A complete lack of a pancreas
The body's cells no longer responding properly to insulin
Too much insulin being produced from birth
questions.explain: In Type 2 diabetes cells stop responding to insulin; it is linked to obesity and often controlled by diet and exercise.

options: The pancreas not producing enough (or any) insulin
The body's cells not responding to insulin
The kidneys failing to filter glucose
questions.explain: In Type 1 diabetes the pancreas produces little or no insulin, so it is usually treated with insulin injections.

questions.q: Light entering the eye is first refracted (bent) by the:
questions.explain: The transparent cornea does most of the refraction of light as it enters the eye.

questions.q: Which neurone carries impulses from a receptor towards the central nervous system?
questions.explain: Sensory neurones carry impulses from receptors to the CNS.

questions.q: How does the contraceptive pill (containing oestrogen/progesterone) prevent pregnancy?
options: It kills sperm directly in the uterus
It inhibits FSH so no eggs mature
questions.explain: The hormones in the pill inhibit FSH production, so no eggs mature and ovulation does not occur.

options: Cause an egg (in a follicle) to mature in the ovary
questions.explain: FSH, secreted by the pituitary gland, stimulates eggs to mature in the ovaries and triggers oestrogen release.
